what: As the page scrolls vertically, the scene strip pinned to the screen slides sideways, passing like a walk along one long picture. Each scene sets the vertical scroll length by its width ratio (default 1 for all, 1.38 for the wide scene), and the strip follows by inertia, closing 25% of the gap to the target every frame. At scenes marked fixed (hero, about, closing contact), one wheel tick jumps to the next or previous scene in .4s power4.inOut, and elsewhere scrolling is free. When a scene is entered (judged with 15% of the neighboring screens skipped), is-fx-in is added to that scene and [data-fx-part=enter] rises from 4rem below over .9s, and the 01~0N circle indicator paints the current scene, click it to jump to that scene

options.sizes: Scene width ratios (comma-separated), default all 1 — original 1,1,1.38,1.38,1.38,1.38,1.38,1.38,1
options.narrow: Width treated as narrow screen (px), default 768
options.fixed: Scene numbers skipped per wheel tick (from 0, comma-separated) — original 0,1,8. Not intercepted on touch screens
options.lerp: Ratio followed per Frame, default .25 — 1 means immediate (original phone)
options.margin: Scene trigger offset (ratio of screen height), default .15
options.--fx-dur · --fx-ease · --fx-delay: [data-fx-part=[enter] rise length·curve·delay (via style) — original .9s ease, .3s delay spacing
options.[data-fx-part=track]: Row holding the scene (required) — directly below the attached element
options.[data-fx-part=scene]: One scene (required) — directly below the line
options.[data-fx-part=dots]: Empty list to draw indicators in (optional)

note: Wheel skipping in a pinned scene blocks the wheel on the whole document — use it only where a whole page serves as the journey. The scene row is fixed on screen, so other sections placed before or after the pinned element will overlap (the original’s whole page is the journey too)
